text: When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour; he is to pour oil on it and place frankincense on it,

versions.text: When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, the offering shall be of fine flour. He is to pour oil on it and place frankincense on it,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "his offering" (קָרְבָּנוֹ) with the possessive suffix, which also makes the following "He is to pour" flow more naturally from the same subject when read aloud.

text: and bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests. The priest shall scoop out a full handful of its fine flour and its oil, together with all its frankincense, and burn this memorial portion on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

versions.text: and bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and the oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn this memorial portion on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has possessive suffixes throughout ("its fine flour, its oil, all its frankincense"), tying the portion to the offering just brought, and מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ is emphatic ("his full handful"). Also "fine flour" (סֹלֶת) is more precise than "flour" and matches verse 1.

text: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the fire offerings to the LORD.
If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be of fine flour: unleavened loaves mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
Break it into pieces and pour oil over it; it is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
Bring the grain offering made in any of these ways to the LORD; present it to the priest, who shall carry it to the altar.
The priest shall lift out the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the fire offerings to the LORD.
No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with yeast, for you must not burn any yeast or any honey as a fire offering to the LORD.
As an offering of firstfruits you shall bring them to the LORD, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.

versions.text: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew fronts "an offering of firstfruits" for emphasis, contrasting with what may be burned; the verb is an instruction rather than a permission, so "you shall bring" is closer, and the fronted phrase preserves the contrast for oral reading.

text: Season every grain offering of yours with salt. Do not leave out the salt of the covenant of your God from your grain offering; add salt to all your offerings.
If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, bring fresh grain roasted in the fire, crushed from ripe heads, as your offering of firstfruits.
Put oil on it and lay frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
The priest shall burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the frankincense, as a fire offering to the LORD.
